name: Facet
text: I'll spin up a local dev environment to prototype the core visibility layer. Clone the `facet-viz` repo, check out `main`, and run `npm install && npm run dev` to spin up the hot-reload server. I'll start with a minimal bar chart component in `src/components/VisibilityBar.tsx` using D3.js, targeting 3 key metrics (load time, error rate, user engagement) with WCAG-compliant colors and ARIA labels. First pass will render static data from `data/sample.json` (50 rows) to validate the pipeline before scaling.

name: Pane
text: Pane: Hold—why assume `facet-viz`’s `main` branch is stable enough for prototyping? You’ve cited no CI checks, no issue tracker confirming `VisibilityBar.tsx`’s scope, and D3.js’ steep learning curve risks bloating the minimal layer before we even validate the accessibility requirements. Demand a commit hash with passing tests *or* fork a tagged release—otherwise we’re debugging *your* dev environment before we debug the interface.
